lines.text: A stranger sees an ordinary defended town at Langburg: enough on the walls to be serious, not enough to be reassuring.
Langburg sits open. There is no ground here that helps it, and everything the town has must be built rather than found.

lines.poolKey: Invasion & War: walls with NO force
lines.text: The town has the thing that would save it and not the people who would use it, and says so when pressed.
The town's law can name a wrong and cannot keep the person who did it, so it reaches for the purse or the road.
The town could go through a bad season with its arrangements intact, and the people who would have to be paid through one know it.
The town has a place for grain and a place for the ill, and knows exactly what having both is worth.
There is a line around Langburg and it is kept: the gates shut, the works are repaired, and a stranger enters where the town intends him to.
There are people walking the town at Langburg at night, and the town's sense of itself rests more on that than on anything at the gate.
A stranger at Langburg finds a hall whose business is the sort of trouble a garrison is the wrong instrument for, and finds it busy.
The town has no answer to anything it cannot see, and is unprepared rather than protected in that respect.

lines.poolKey: COMPOUND override (a crisis stress has rewritten the label)
lines.text: The ordinary safety of Langburg has stopped applying. Whatever the town was, the crisis on it now is what governs the streets.

lines.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
lines.text: What the town says about its own safety at Langburg is what the town says on a first acquaintance, and a longer one would be a different account.

lines.poolKey: Logistics & Supply: Granary with road supply
lines.text: An interruption on the roads to Langburg does not reach the table, and the granary is the reason rather than the roads.
Langburg's gates (if walled) stands better than the watch that should man it; stone keeps itself, and wages do not.
What Langburg's defenses are ordinarily worth does not describe the town at present; there is a crisis on it, and the arrangements have been rebuilt around the crisis.
Langburg is under real pressure and is not in danger of ending; the posture has changed and the town has not.
There is magic at Langburg and the town does not rest on it. Losing every practitioner here would be a loss and not a collapse.
The road runs past Langburg and Langburg takes very little from it; the traffic is real and the town has stayed outside it.
Langburg keeps no market worth the name; exchange here happens at doorsteps and in yards, at the scale the town actually needs.

lines.poolKey: the MARGINAL arm: neither verdict returned
lines.text: Whether Langburg holds together is not a settled question. The pieces mostly fit, and the places where they do not are the places worth reading.
The town was read once, carefully, and the reading has not been repeated.
Langburg was never founded so much as agreed to, one household at a time.
The Guild Council's writ runs shorter at Langburg each season, and what the rolls show is not defiance so much as delay, which comes to the same figure at collection.
What the Guild Council has lost at Langburg it has lost to the crime returns. A town that does not feel safe stops crediting whoever is meant to keep it so.
What is settled at Langburg is the hall and only the hall; the town's steadiness is a statement about who answers, and not about what the answers will be.
Nobody at Langburg needs the trouble explained to them; it is recent enough that the town simply refers to it and moves on.

lines.poolKey: legitimacyHold: public rejection is breaking the hold
lines.text: The town has turned on whoever sits at Langburg, and the turning is doing more damage to the hold than any rival has managed.

lines.poolKey: governing body name: a SLOT, never a baked noun
lines.text: A stranger who addresses the Guild Council at Langburg by any other title is corrected, politely and immediately.
A stranger at Langburg cannot work out who is aligned with whom, and the reason is that nobody is.
Langburg manages. The market trade covers what the town needs and leaves a little over, and the little over is what the year gets argued about.
Nothing about Langburg's condition asks to be remarked on. The town supports itself and has a little in hand.
Langburg is not hungry and has no cushion. A shock to the fields or the road would be felt inside a season.

lines.poolKey: INCOME MIX: a broad spread, no leader
lines.text: Langburg would barely notice losing any single trade and could not replace several, which is a different exposure from the obvious one.

lines.poolKey: TRADE PROFILE: exports and imports both present
lines.text: Everybody here knows what leaves and what arrives, because the same carts do both.
What passes for a shadow economy here has never grown into one. There is unlicensed trade and nothing organised behind it.
There is nothing between this town and the horizon but what the town has planted, and the town knows both halves of that.

lines.poolKey: ECONOMIC STRENGTHS: the roster is populated
lines.text: Langburg has more than one thing it is good at, and the list is short enough that everybody here could recite it.

lines.poolKey: STRATEGIC VALUE: the generator's assessment, framed
lines.text: What Langburg is worth to anybody else is a separate question from what it is worth to itself, and the two answers are not close.
This is the trade the town is actually built on, and the town has taken it as far as it goes.
Minor shadow activity. Petty theft and small-scale unlicensed trade. An inconvenience, not a structural threat.
